title: Tooling: 3.57x faster complete T74 native replay with unchanged exact coverage
body:
The complete PR2751 T74 native replay spends most of its time compiling exact Clifford states. This opt-in runner integrates Charles Bethin's PR662 gate tables and Ali Romman's PR1029 sparse evaluator into the two Clifford-using stages while retaining the unchanged independent warp checks and every original native control.

**Tooling improvement; no new κ.** Three alternating pairs on the same base word measured a **3.57× complete-native speedup**, median **306.7s → 85.9s** (72% less wall time). All eleven native artifacts matched in every pair after only documented elapsed-time and verified gzip-container normalization; phase recipes were byte-identical. This is a measured native-verification improvement, not a whole-project or multiplication-runtime claim.

Validation and scope:

- Fresh complete base and extra provider replays; the extra runs from a Git-free copy in a path with spaces.
- All 84 inherited negative controls retained (46 local, 25 wrapper, 13 recipe), including the independent all 512-column warp checks.
- 1,488 dense/sparse exact-state comparisons plus 18 new boundary controls for altered source, fixture, word, recipe, receipt, optimized Python and output reuse.
- Exact source closure, both fixtures, complete six-sample benchmark and reference digests are in `research/t74-native-fast/`. No saved native result is reused. The full supplier/hosting/outer admission remains separate.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 and numpy 2.2.6:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/t74-native-fast
```

The scientific base is `2d3af1ba7e28b74248b47381768e5b116078ba1c`; the branch was synchronized to canonical main `936fac15b1b1b59dc5285c713a77f9f3c07b2906` before submission. Native sources and both actual input words are pinned through PR2751 `4cfbb0cc8314d7fb4e8e754545a49a42eb590a69` and PR2679. Relevant sources, priorities and selected record were unchanged by the refresh.

This contributes current T74 integration and complete-pipeline evidence, not a new sparse algorithm. PR1041's older U8 runner and Victor Li's related PR2329 multicold production integration are credited. PR2226's borrowing operators, the Rohan Arun/icekylinx/DreamingOfClouds native lineage, Philippe Van Velzen's source snapshot and the complete PR2751 predecessor notices are retained. Frozen sources and the selected frontier are unchanged.

Coordination: [discussion #2755](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2755). Final overlap search covered all 710 open PRs, the earlier complete discussion snapshot and a fresh 40-discussion fallback; limits are recorded in `FRESHNESS.json`.

Prepared by Tekalign (@tekuuu) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0. Author-checked evidence; independent human review remains welcome.

Submission-time follow-up: [PR2766](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2766) (`e6df920cd0110e4b629e2ad84eddcb539001e174`, David Arias) and [PR2767](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2767) (`e8b771ba132fe632796b28c1742a8d096c04519f`, Jeremy Kothe) appeared during final verification with conditional κ claims around0.001717256973467. PR2766 explicitly distinguishes this native-acceleration scope. Those newer constructions were not audited in this tooling round: our measured timings and equality receipts remain tied to the two exact PR2751 words, and do not assert successor-word performance.
